articles.title: Matt LaFleur confirms suspicion about Packers' coaching staff after Vikings loss, delivering an unpopular answer
articles.summary: Offensive line coach Luke Butkus has faced heavy scrutiny all season, and the Packers head coach addressed his status after a 30-10 loss to Minnesota.
articles.body:
Offensive line coach Luke Butkus has faced heavy scrutiny all season, and the Packers head coach addressed his status after a 30-10 loss to Minnesota.

Green Bay Packers head coach Matt LaFleur met with the media Monday after a 30-10 loss to the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday. The most pressing question was about the coaching staff , particularly offensive line coach Luke Butkus. LaFleur does not plan to make any changes, though. Butkus will stay in his role through the rest of the season. The offensive line has drawn much of the scrutiny after the loss to Minnesota. Still, the Packers' head coach made his position clear when asked if Butkus was the right man for the job.

LaFleur did not hesitate with his answer about his offensive line coach, who's been the position coach for the past five seasons, saying he's the right person for the job. "Yeah, I think he is," LaFleur said. "First of all, it starts with me. I have to be better, the staff has to be better, Butkus has to be better, and our players have to go out there, execute, play with great technique and fundamentals, and do their jobs."

LaFleur was then asked to justify that answer and explain why he still believes Butkus fits the role. He pointed to the offensive line coach's body of work. "Because he was the same guy when we were rolling," the coach explained. "It's easy to point fingers and assign blame, but the blame goes to everybody. We're all in this together. Again, it starts with me and extends to everyone else. It's on the coaches and players collectively." That answer frames the offensive line's problems as a shared responsibility. LaFleur puts himself first in line, then the staff and the players. In his view, firing one assistant would not fix a unit that has struggled across the board.

Luke Butkus has been with the Packers since 2019. He spent his first three seasons as an assistant offensive line coach. Green Bay then promoted him to offensive line coach in 2022, when former offensive line coach Adam Stenavich became the offensive coordinator. The results haven't been great . The Packers have had problems developing offensive linemen over the past few seasons, and the unit's play has been a weak spot in 2026. In LaFleur's offensive scheme, the line should set the ceiling for everything else on offense. In reality, it has lowered its floor. Even so, LaFleur believes Butkus has shown enough during his time in Green Bay. The coach sees him as capable of being what the Packers need at that position. The reference to "when we were rolling" shows LaFleur is weighing the good stretches alongside the bad ones, rather than judging Butkus on a single bad stretch.

The Green Bay Packers have a 34% chance to make the NFL playoffs and a 1% chance to win Super Bowl LXI, according to the A to Z Sports NFL Playoff Predictor (updated Mon, Nov 16).

That wasn't necessarily a surprise. Matt LaFleur has been willing to make changes on his coaching staff in the offseason, but he remains conservative in that regard. During the season, he has never fired an assistant coach. That approach won't change with Butkus. Despite all the concerns about how the offensive line has performed and how the unit has been coached this season, Green Bay will ride it out with the same staff.

For the most part, that philosophy prioritizes continuity and accountability over reactive moves. LaFleur's message is consistent with how he has run the Packers since he took over. For better or worse. The decision also means the pressure falls squarely on the current group to improve. If the offensive line doesn't take a step forward over the final stretch, the conversation about Butkus will return in the offseason, when LaFleur has historically been more open to change. Until then, the head coach has drawn his line, and the offensive line coach stays in place.

articles.title: NFL Draft 2027 Scouting Report for South Carolina Edge Dylan Stewart
articles.summary: Dylan Stewart has the best traits of any edge defender in the 2026 NFL Draft class, possessing a good frame and elite athleticism that will translate to the next level. However, his technique was a work in progress heading into the season, and a back injury and suspension have limited his playing time this year.
articles.body: Dylan Stewart has the best traits of any edge defender in the 2026 NFL Draft class, possessing a good frame and elite athleticism that will translate to the next level. However, his technique was a work in progress heading into the season, and a back injury and suspension have limited his playing time this year. A 5-star recruit and the No. 15 player overall in the 2024 high school class, the 6'5", 250-pound pass rusher was an immediate starter at South Carolina. He posted 23 tackles, 10.5 tackles for loss and 6.5 sacks to earn first-team All-SEC and Freshman All-American honors in 13 games as a true freshman. Year two is when Stewart's back issues started. Although he missed only one game, the Washington, D.C., native played through the injury and posted 33 tackles, 12.0 TFLs, and 4.5 sacks. That resulted in second-team All-SEC and honorable mention All-American recognition. Matt Holder has been a part of B/R's Scouting Department for five seasons. He also writes about the Las Vegas Raiders and NFL draft for SB Nation's Silver and Black Pride , and co-hosts a YouTube Channel, Tape Don't Lie , providing film breakdowns and more draft prospect analysis. Stewart has decent size for an NFL edge defender and a good frame with room for growth and plenty of athleticism to still be effective after adding mass. Reportedly has near-34-inch arms, according to Pro Football Network . Explosive off the line of scrimmage to threaten offensive tackles with speed around the edge as a pass-rusher. Very good quickness to beat offensive tackles across their faces. Has flashed the ability to set up his pass rush moves by stemming or getting to square and giving himself a two-way go. Decent long-arm, swim and hand swipe moves. Bendy to turn tight corners at the top of the rush. Very effective looper on line games with the lateral movement skills to gain ground vertically while moving laterally and has very good closing speed on the quarterback. Knack for getting strip sacks. He has eight career forced fumbles as of Oct. 21, 2026. As a run defender, he has the strength and physicality to take on blocks from tight ends. When taking on pullers, he uses low pad level and is physical to create stalemates as the force player in the run fit. Flashed the ability to use his quickness to defeat blocks. Has the speed and bend to make tackles near the line of scrimmage when unblocked on the backside of zone runs. Stewart will have to answer questions about his character and coachability after the incident at Alabama that led to his one-game suspension. Could afford to add some extra size and upper body strength to get extension when taking on base blocks from offensive linemen. Late or slow to recognize run concepts, which can lead to him getting reached/sealed inside against outside zone runs. He also doesn't show great gap discipline by trying to work inside the block instead of running his feet and stretching it out. Use of hands is still a work in progress as a pass-rusher. His timing can be late and is inconsistent to "beat the hands, beat the man" regularly. Also, can be better at working the offensive lineman's hands after contact to get clean wins. Pass-rush lane integrity is subpar; he will lose outside containment on the edge occassionally. Back injury has the potential to be a medical red flag since it has lingered from one season to the next. Grade, Rank, and Play-Style Archetype PLAY-STYLE ARCHETYPE : Highly Athletic Edge-Rusher (Brian Burns to Josh Sweat) Workout numbers and data will be added at a later date.

articles.title: NFL Draft 2027 Scouting Report for Georgia LB Chris Cole
articles.summary: Chris Cole is a rare athlete for a linebacker and has shown that he can make a significant impact on all three phases of the game defensively. The Georgia product was primarily used in passing situations previously but has taken on an expanded role in 2026 to enter the first-round discussion when it comes to the NFL Draft.
articles.body:
Chris Cole is a rare athlete for a linebacker and has shown that he can make a significant impact on all three phases of the game defensively. The Georgia product was primarily used in passing situations previously but has taken on an expanded role in 2026 to enter the first-round discussion when it comes to the NFL Draft.

A 5-star recruit in the 2024 high school class, Cole was more of a role player or rotational linebacker during his first two years with the Bulldogs. He collected 75 tackles, nine tackles for loss , 4.5 sacks, three passes defended and two fumble recoveries (one for a touchdown) in 28 games (one start) during that time frame.

The Salem, Virginia native earned an SEC All-Freshman Team bid, and his emergence as a starter during the 2026 campaign has fueled his breakout performance. The 6'3", 235-pound linebacker has become a more complete player, giving him every-down potential at the next level.

Matt Holder has been a part of B/R's Scouting Department for five seasons. He also writes about the Las Vegas Raiders and NFL draft for SB Nation's Silver and Black Pride , and co-hosts a YouTube Channel, Tape Don't Lie , providing film breakdowns and more draft prospect analysis.

Cole has good size and length for an NFL linebacker and has room for growth on his frame. Reportedly has 33-inch arms, according to On3's Jake Rowe .

Very good athlete who has great speed and lateral movement skills to close or cover ground in a hurry and navigate blocks or the trash in the running game.

Athleticism allows him to be effective in man coverage against running backs and tight ends.

Uses his hands well in coverage to help stay in phase or disrupt the timing of routes.

Decent ball skills/production with six career PDs, including three in 2026, as of Oct. 14, 2026.

Speed and good pursuit angles allow him to make chase-down tackles. That also gives him elite sideline-to-sideline range.

Instincts as a run defender have grown with an increased role in 2026, showing the ability to beat offensive linemen to the spot against gap runs.

Uses his agility to make offensive linemen miss and defeat blocks.

Good tackler, he breaks down in space well, wraps up consistently and arm length increases tackle radius.

Has a good hand-swipe move and bend as a pass-rusher to be an effective blitzer or rush off the edge.

Cole is only a one-year college starter and wasn't used on a lot of early downs to begin his career.

Could afford to add some strength to be better at holding up at the point of attack and anchoring when taking on blocks from offensive linemen.

Isn't very physical at the point of attack either.

Doesn't have much force when coming downhill.

Eye discipline and awareness in coverage could use some work; he's prone to occasional coverage busts and doesn't show the instincts to quickly recognize passing concepts/route combinations.

Will leave his man instead of plastering on scramble drills.

More of a long strider than a short-area burst type of athlete, which can impact his ability to click and close in coverage.

PLAY-STYLE ARCHETYPE : Highly athletic and versatile linebacker (Alex Anzalone to Quay Walker)

articles.title: NFL Draft 2027 Scouting Report for Alabama WR Ryan-Coleman Williams
articles.summary: Ryan Coleman-Williams is one of the nation's most dynamic and explosive run-after-catch threats.
articles.body:
Ryan Coleman-Williams is one of the nation's most dynamic and explosive run-after-catch threats.

He burst onto the college football scene as a 17-year-old freshman phenom. Williams took the SEC by storm, using his incredible physical ability and athleticism to flip field position on offense.

Coleman-Williams reclassified from 2025 to 2024, becoming a top-10 national player and a 5-star recruit in the 2024 class.

Dame is the lead host of the Locked On NFL Draft podcast. Previously, he spent three years as a senior draft analyst for The Draft Network while evaluating draft prospects as the founder of The Scouting Room .

Dangerous playmaker with the football; Creates YAC with outstanding post-catch speed and acceleration.

Deceptive route salesman; makes routes look the same until the breakpoint.

He excels at creating separation with route tempo, patience, and suddenness.

Open-field elusiveness to make the first defender miss after the catch.

High football IQ with recognizing coverages and defensive backs' leverage post-snap. He finds and exploits soft spots vs. zone.

Securing passes and limiting drops: must learn to stay grounded through the catch instead of jumping for it.

Slender build/frame creates questions regarding playing through contact at the catch point.

Bigger/strong corners can limit his explosive factor with physical contact at the LOS and mid-route, preventing Coleman-Williams from winning the foot race.

Limited wingspan/arm length creates difficulty winning at the catch point.

Player Archetype : An explosive three-level receiver. He runs routes with nuance and detail. In space, he brings dynamism after the catch to the passing offense. He won't often be called on to win contested/jump balls. Similar to the New Orleans Saints' star Chris Olave.

articles.title: NFL Draft 2027 Scouting Report for Ole Miss DL Will Echoles
articles.summary: Will Echoles is an elite run defender who can defeat every type of block with his combination of size, strength and movement skills. The 6'3", 315-pound defensive tackle also offers some alignment versatility and has the traits to grow as a pass-rusher at the next level. However, he'll likely enter the NFL as more of a two-down contributor.
articles.body:
Will Echoles is an elite run defender who can defeat every type of block with his combination of size, strength and movement skills. The 6'3", 315-pound defensive tackle also offers some alignment versatility and has the traits to grow as a pass-rusher at the next level. However, he'll likely enter the NFL as more of a two-down contributor.

A 4-star recruit in the 2024 high school class, Echoles played sparingly as a true freshman before breaking out in year two at Ole Miss during the Rebels' College Football Playoff run. He logged 68 tackles, 11.5 for loss, five sacks and five passes defended to earn first-team All-SEC and fourth-team All-American honors.

Matt Holder has been a part of B/R's Scouting Department for five seasons. He also writes about the Las Vegas Raiders and NFL draft for SB Nation's Silver and Black Pride , and co-hosts a YouTube Channel, Tape Don't Lie , providing film breakdowns and more draft prospect analysis.

Echoles has good size and frame, with a thick lower half to help stay in his gap against the run.

Quick to recognize blocking schemes to put himself in a good position to take on blocks.

Strong at the point of attack to rest the line of scrimmage, get extension against and stand up interior offensive linemen.

Takes on blocks with decent pad level and a wide base to help absorb contact and maintain gap control when taking on combo blocks.

Runs his feet and has good lateral movement skills to avoid getting reached.

Can stack and shed, has flashed swim and rip moves to defeat blocks, and occasionally splits combos to make tackles near the line of scrimmage.

Shows the quickness and agility to work the edges as a pass-rusher if his hand usage improves/becomes more accurate.

Gets his hands up when he doesn't win as a pass-rusher and has a knack for batting passes at the line.

Echoles doesn't show many pass-rush moves that will translate to the next level.

Pad level rises when rushing the passer and lacks consistent explosion off the line of scrimmage to consistently push the pocket when bull rushing.

Accuracy with his hands as a pass-rusher is a work in progress.

Doesn't work the offensive lineman's hands when rushing the passer.

PLAY-STYLE ARCHETYPE : Run-first 3-technique (Jeffery Simmons to A'Shawn Robinson)

articles.title: Aidan Hutchinson Injured Celebrating, Latest on Diagnosis and Timeline to Return for Lions Star
articles.summary: Detroit Lions star Aidan Hutchinson has been diagnosed with a torn ACL suffered during Sunday's game against the New England Patriots, head coach Dan Campbell confirmed on Tuesday.
articles.body:
Detroit Lions star Aidan Hutchinson has been diagnosed with a torn ACL suffered during Sunday's game against the New England Patriots, head coach Dan Campbell confirmed on Tuesday.

NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and ESPN's Adam Schefter reported Monday that Hutchinson would be expected to miss the rest of the season after the severity was confirmed:

Tom Pelissero of The Ringer and Netflix first reported Sunday that Hutchinson suffered a "significant" knee injury.

Hutchinson was hurt when he landed awkwardly after celebrating a sack on New England's opening drive of the first quarter. He was subsequently ruled out .

Rapoport described Hutchinson as doing a "full Gramatica." Former Arizona Cardinals kicker Bill Gramatica tore his ACL while celebrating a made field goal in a 2001 game.

Hutchinson enjoyed a return to form in 2025 after fractures to his tibia and fibula limited him to five games a season earlier. He had 14.5 sacks en route to earning a second Pro Bowl nod and finishing fifth in the Defensive Player of the Year voting.

The fifth-year pass-rusher was delivering more of the same through the Lions' first eight games. He had five sacks and 18 hits on the quarterback, and he made his presence felt early Sunday by bringing down Patriots quarterback Drake Maye.

After Week 10, Detroit is allowing 332.3 yards per game, which ranks 17th in the league, and ranks near last in pass defense (241.9). That's despite totaling the third-most sacks (32) in the NFL.

articles.title: From 0-8 to finally finding a formula, the Chargers’ victory over Baltimore could change the direction of their season
articles.summary: The Chargers have a win at last. They beat the Baltimore Ravens 23-20 on Monday Night Football, ending an 0-8 start that began back in September.
articles.body: The Chargers have a win at last. They beat the Baltimore Ravens 23-20 on Monday Night Football, ending an 0-8 start that began back in September. Justin Herbert scored on a 22-yard scramble in the first quarter, Cameron Dicker kicked three field goals, and Los Angeles did not turn the ball over once. Baltimore piled up more yards and threw 49 times, but the Chargers never trailed and stayed ahead after the Ravens cut it to three with 10:23 left. The record is 1-8. The Jets come to town on Nov. 22.The formula that ended the Chargers’ 0-8 startThe plan was not complicated. Run the ball, protect it, take the points when a drive stalls. Los Angeles carried 34 times for 160 yards, an average of 4.7, and threw only 18 passes. Two of its touchdowns came on the ground, Herbert’s scramble and a one-yard run by Hampton late in the second quarter. The box score also lists seven scrambles, which tells you the Chargers were happy to let their quarterback improvise.Ball security was the quiet edge. The Chargers had no turnovers. Baltimore had two, an interception and a lost fumble. In a three-point game, that gap mattered a lot.Baltimore moved the ball through the air. It completed 33 of 49 passes for 340 yards, and the Ravens finished with 347 total yards to the Chargers’ 287. But the run game never showed up. Baltimore ran 15 times for 16 yards, and two of those carries were Henry’s touchdown runs from two yards and one yard out. Baltimore trailed 17-10 at halftime, and 49 passes against 15 runs suggests an offense chasing the game. The Chargers also forced four three-and-outs and broke up 10 passes, which helps explain why all those yards became only 20 points.What the win does and does not changeOne win does not fix a season. The Chargers lost their first eight games by 12, 12, 8, 7, 6, 16, 15 and 22 points, the last of those a 44-22 home loss to Houston. Eight days later they were beating a Baltimore team that had the yards and still came up short.The defense deserves a share of the credit. It hit the quarterback nine times, sacked him twice and picked off one pass. After Baltimore made it 23-20, nobody scored again. Los Angeles also won small field-position fights: two of its six punts finished inside the 20, and Baltimore had none.Dicker’s kicks from 38, 34 and 35 yards made the difference. Baltimore’s kicker hit from 26 and 36.The schedule offers a quick test of whether this was a template or a one-off. The Jets visit on Nov. 22, and the stats feed had Los Angeles at 62.2 percent to win before that game. The Patriots follow on Sunday Night Football on Nov. 29. articles.title: Aidan Hutchinson: Detroit Lions star out for season after celebration injury
articles.summary: Detroit Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson will miss the rest of the NFL season after sustaining a serious knee injury while celebrating.
articles.body:
Detroit Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson will miss the rest of the NFL season after sustaining a serious knee injury while celebrating.

Hutchinson, 26, jumped in the air after bringing down New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye in the first quarter of the Lions' 35-10 win in Munich.

The 2022 second overall pick fell to the ground shortly after landing, clutching his right knee.

Hutchinson walked to the sideline after medical treatment on the field but did not return to the game - and has torn his anterior cruciate ligament.

It is the second season-ending injury of Hutchinson career - but Lions head coach Dan Campbell has no plans to stop his players from expressing themselves.

"I hate it. I think we all understand what it is, and let's be smart, but no, I'm not gonna say 'nobody celebrates any more'," Campbell said.

"The number of moves that I've seen 'Hutch' make and the number of plyometrics, explosive movements, the spins, the one-leg lateral movements, lateral balances... it was one of those things, man."

This was the sixth regular-season NFL game to be played in Germany and the third to be held at Bayern Munich's Allianz Arena.

The Lions' win means they are top of the NFC North and have the second-best record in the conference.

Hutchinson is regarded as one of the premier pass rushers in the NFL, and is currently tied for 13th in the league with six sacks this season.

Campbell is confident Hutchinson will come back stronger on his return from the injury setback.

"He's such a phenomenal player, an impact player, but more importantly he's an unbelievable team-mate and he's one of our captains," Campbell added.

"What a hell of a year he was having. He's just improved every year and to come off the injury he had [in 2024].

"This guy will overcome this and he will come back better than he was. It's just the way he is, it's the way he's wired."

Patriots' Maye remained in Germany after tackle

Maye reportedly sustained a fractured ankle during the tackle Hutchinson was celebrating, so the Patriots will be concerned the quarterback could miss the remainder of the season too.

Head coach Mike Vrabel confirmed Maye had remained in Germany, telling Boston radio station WEEI the 24-year-old stayed "out of caution".

After being beaten by the Seattle Seahawks in the 2026 Super Bowl, the Patriots are second in the AFC East having won five and lost five this season.

Their chances of reaching the playoffs will likely be reliant on securing a wildcard place as the Buffalo Bills currently top the division with an 8-1 record.

articles.summary: 1XBET nos ofrece las mejores cuotas del fútbol americano
articles.body: El panorama de la Super Bowl LXI ha cambiado por completo. Los Rams comenzaron el curso como grandes favoritos, con cuotas cercanas a 6 en las casas de apuestas estadounidenses, pero una plaga de lesiones y un rendimiento por debajo de lo esperado de Matthew Stafford los han llevado a un 6-4 y a pelear por entrar en playoffs. En su lugar, 1XBet sitúa en lo más alto de las apuestas deportivas a dos equipos que llevan semanas siendo los mejores sobre el campo. Los Buffalo Bills son los nuevos favoritos, a cuota 6.3. Con un balance de 8-1, empatan con San Francisco como el mejor registro de la NFL, y Josh Allen llega sano y en plenitud. El conjunto de Buffalo es, además, el que más caminos ofrece hacia la gran final: aparece en siete de los principales cruces posibles del mercado de enfrentamientos. Su cuota refleja una probabilidad cercana al 16%, y el gran reto sigue siendo el mismo de siempre: los Bills no llegan a una Super Bowl desde 1994. Muy cerca aparecen los San Francisco 49ers, a cuota 6.85. Brock Purdy está jugando a un nivel de MVP y el equipo mantiene un 8-1, aunque su racha incluyó la primera derrota de la temporada ante los Falcons y una lista de lesionados que no deja de crecer. Es el favorito en algunas casas de apuestas de EE. UU., y su precio en 1xBet es la señal de que el mercado ve la pelea entre ambos como una cuestión de matices. Los Kansas City Chiefs ocupan el tercer puesto, a cuota 8.7. Con Patrick Mahomes sano tras superar la grave lesión de rodilla del año pasado, los campeones de tantos años siguen siendo un rival que nadie quiere ver en enero. Su cuota premia la experiencia de un equipo acostumbrado a las eliminatorias, aunque también refleja que esta vez no parten como los grandes dominadores de la conferencia. Los Jacksonville Jaguars son la gran revelación, a cuota 8.9. El conjunto de Florida ha escalado posiciones de forma notable en las últimas semanas, después de reforzar su defensa en el cierre del mercado con Jessie Bates III, Davon Godchaux y Jordan Davis. Esos movimientos le han llevado a ser el tercero en muchos mercados internacionales, por delante de equipos con más tradición, y su cuota es la de un aspirante que ya no sorprende a nadie. Los Rams cierran la lista, a cuota 13.7. Han caído de ser los grandes favoritos a convertirse en un equipo que lucha por entrar en playoffs, tras perder a piezas como Puka Nacua, Davante Adams y otros jugadores clave. Aun así, no conviene descartarlos: llegaron a encadenar cuatro victorias seguidas después de un inicio de 2-4, y con Sean McVay en el banquillo su techo sigue siendo alto si recuperan a sus estrellas. Su precio es el de un aspirante de riesgo, con un premio superior al de los cuatro primeros.

articles.title: Jerry Jones Addresses Christian Parker's Hot Seat After Cowboys Struggle in 49ers Loss
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones was asked during a Tuesday appearance on the Shan & RJ radio show on 105.3 The Fan whether the team is considering any adjustments or a change in responsibilities regarding defensive coordinator Christian Parker's role.
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones was asked during a Tuesday appearance on the Shan & RJ radio show on 105.3 The Fan whether the team is considering any adjustments or a change in responsibilities regarding defensive coordinator Christian Parker's role.

"We're talking about that, but I'm not going to talk about it here, but we are talking about those things," Jones said (h/t Josh Alper of Pro Football Talk).

The Cowboys allowed 584 yards in a 46-40 home loss to the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday, dropping the team to 4-6.

Sunday represented the Dallas defense's low point, with the team allowing three touchdowns of 66 or more yards. Dallas has now allowed the second-most yards per play (6.1) and the third-most points per game (28.2) in the NFL.

On Monday, Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer was asked whether the team remains confident in Parker.

"We'll still working through the process," Schottenheimer told reporters . "Talking to the guys is the first step. At the end of the day, there's a lot of things we need to clean up as a football team. That starts with me. You look at this game, the positives. Five sacks team that had been sacked eight times — you get five sacks. Probably missed another three or four, could have been almost double digits. But at the end of the day, the tackling and some of the coverage stuff led to the explosives. We're taking a deep dive, we're looking at everything."

Schottenheimer was then asked if the team could make a change at defensive coordinator.

"I'm not saying that," Schottenheimer said. "I'm saying we're still in the process of going through all the film and evaluation of where we stand today."

The 34-year-old Parker arrived in town last offseason after two seasons as the Philadelphia Eagles' defensive passing game coordinator and defensive backs coach. He won a Super Bowl with the 2024 Eagles thanks in part to the defensive backs' great performance that season.

Dallas has made major additions on defense dating back to the 2025 midseason, when the Cowboys traded for defensive lineman Quinnen Williams. They include cornerback Joey Porter Jr. (via trade from the Pittsburgh Steelers), safety Caleb Downs and edge-rusher Malachi Lawrence (via the first round of the 2026 draft).

Ultimately, Dallas' defense has struggled for three years running now, with the team allowing the second-most points per game in 2024 and the most points per game in 2025.

The next two weeks are against teams ranked 28th (Tennessee Titans) and 30th (Eagles) in points per game. Kickoff against Tennessee is slated for 1 p.m. ET on Sunday.

articles.title: La NFL no para de crecer: "Seguramente haya más partidos en España"
articles.standfirst: Jozy Altidore, Diego Paz y Gerardo Riquelme analizan en el Business Sport Forum cómo convertir el tirón de los partidos en Madrid en afición y oportunidades para los jugadores de aquí
articles.summary: Jozy Altidore, Diego Paz y Gerardo Riquelme analizan en el Business Sport Forum cómo convertir el tirón de los partidos en Madrid en afición y oportunidades para los jugadores de aquí
articles.body: La NFL ya ha conseguido que dos partidos de su temporada regular se jueguen en el Santiago Bernabéu. El siguiente reto es que parte de ese público siga pendiente del fútbol americano cuando la liga vuelva a Estados Unidos. Sobre cómo prolongar el efecto de esos partidos debatieron en el Business Sport Forum Jozy Altidore, socio de los Buffalo Bills, que intervino por videoconferencia, Diego Paz, jugador de fútbol americano, y Gerardo Riquelme, subdirector de MARCA. El coloquio estuvo moderado por Víctor M. Osorio, de EXPANSIÓN. Riquelme vio en la vuelta de la NFL a Madrid una señal de que su expansión en Europa se está asentando. Tras el duelo entre los Washington Commanders y los Miami Dolphins del año pasado, el Bernabéu acogió este año el Cincinnati Bengals-Atlanta Falcons. El subdirector de MARCA cree que España tiene opciones de repetir la próxima temporada y destacó el poder de convocatoria de una cita que atrae a aficionados de Francia, Reino Unido, Portugal o Italia. "Ya se vive una experiencia más allá de lo que es solo un partido", explicó un Riquelme que ve otro partido de la NFL "en España, aunque seguramente más en Barcelona que en Madrid porque se 'estrenará' el Camp Nou". Altidore puso el foco en lo que ganan las franquicias al salir de Estados Unidos. Los encuentros les permiten dar a conocer sus marcas en otros mercados y movilizar a seguidores estadounidenses que aprovechan el viaje para pasar unos días fuera siguiendo a su equipo. El socio de los Bills apuntó también a la necesidad de contar con más jugadores europeos que sirvan de referencia para los jóvenes. Comparó la forma en que se transmite la afición a una franquicia de la NFL de una generación a otra con lo que ocurre en España con el Real Madrid o el Barcelona. Paz llevó el debate a los campos de entrenamiento. "Invertir tanto en instalaciones como, lo primordial, invertir en preparadores, en gente que capte talento y lo desarrolle", reclamó. El jugador cree que las visitas de la NFL dan visibilidad a las ligas española y europea y consiguen que los ojeadores se fijen más en sus jugadores. También recordó la oportunidad que tuvo de hacer una prueba con los New England Patriots después de su temporada con Rhein Fire. Allí pudo entrenarse junto a jugadores a los que hasta entonces veía por televisión. Lo que más le llamó la atención fue su dedicación. ¿Y qué le diría a alguien que se siente por primera vez a ver un partido? Paz admitió que las reglas exigen paciencia y explicó qué le enganchó a él. Cada jugador tiene una tarea y buena parte de lo que decide una jugada sucede lejos del balón. "Los que jugamos al fútbol americano lo llamamos el ajedrez humano".

articles.title: Kirk Cousins' career: Chains, tears and more money than Tom Brady
articles.summary: Cousins career has twisted and turned and finally landed back in Minnesota, where the Vikings are hoping he can be their savior.
articles.body:
There are quarterbacks like Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes, who achieve stardom and become synonymous with one team. There are quarterbacks like … well, we don't need to name them, but quarterbacks who never capitalize on their draft-day promise and fade into the ether. And then there's Kirk Cousins, whose career has swooped and swerved in a way he never can on the field.

From spare-parts draft pick to decade-long starter, from chain-wearing goof to one of the highest-paid players in the history of the sport, Cousins' career is a study in improbability, and naturally, he's just landed in the unlikeliest position of all — on track for true postseason success. You like that?

Cousins' story has played out in front of NFL audiences since 2012, when Washington drafted him in the fourth round, 102nd overall — exactly 100 spots behind fellow Washington pick Robert Griffin III. From the start, then, he was a second option, the "Is Pepsi OK?" of quarterbacks. But when Griffin struggled with injuries and poor performance, Cousins stepped in, taking over in Washington in 2015 and holding the starting role there for three seasons.

That 2015 season launched the first of Cousins' multiple memes, and the one likely to follow him the rest of his life: the "You like that?!" he bellowed in Week 7 after Washington overcame a 24-point deficit to beat Tampa Bay. For an affable guy who seemed like he'd be at ease in musical theater — because that's exactly what he was — the declaration was shocking, out of character and absolutely welcome.

"It honestly just came out of having a chip on your shoulder, trying to prove yourself and having a lot of passion," Cousins said later that season. "I think it's been a good rallying cry for our team. Looking back at a great accomplishment, just saying, 'You like that.' It's a stamp of approval on a good performance, kinda two thumbs up."

And it worked. Like hearing your grandmother curse, "You like that?!" was unexpected but also unforgettable, and it helped propel Washington to an NFC East title.

That marked the first distinctive signpost in Cousins' career, but over the next two seasons, the strangeness of Cousins' NFL arc began to take shape. Washington franchise-tagged him twice, the first quarterback ever to receive that designation, kicking the is-he-good-or-isn't-he can down the road for multiple seasons.

The sides parted ways prior to the 2018 season, and the Vikings signed Cousins to a fully guaranteed three-year deal worth $84 million — at the time, both the largest fully guaranteed contract and the largest annual value deal. Cousins and the Vikings weren't able to ascend to the next level during this era, though there were highlights — Minnesota's most recent playoff win came under Cousins in January 2020, to start. He rolled out the "Kirko Chains" persona in 2022, and along with new head coach Kevin O'Connell engineered the largest comeback in NFL history, rallying from a 33-0 deficit against the Colts later that same year.

Cousins tore his right Achilles in October 2023, setting up his next great career swerve. Atlanta, in desperate need of a quarterback in the post-Matt Ryan era, signed Cousins in 2024 to a four-year, $180 million deal with $100 million guaranteed. But Atlanta was apparently in such desperate need of a quarterback that the Falcons also used a first-round draft pick on Michael Penix Jr. about six weeks after signing Cousins.

Another stop where the team was only one foot in on Cousins.

Erratic play and injury issues dogged Cousins during his brief tenure in Atlanta, and he exchanged the starting role with Penix several times. The arrival of a new coaching regime in 2026 meant the end of Cousins' tenure, and he made another leap, this time to Las Vegas to start and mentor No. 1 overall draft pick Fernando Mendoza.

For the first few games of the 2026 season, the Cousins move seemed like genius: Las Vegas went 3-0 to start the season, albeit against the Dolphins, Chargers and Saints. A four-loss streak followed, and at the trade deadline, the Raiders sent Cousins back to Minnesota for a 2027 third-round pick.

Cousins' first Vikings tenure ended in Green Bay's Lambeau Field where he tore his Achilles in 2023, and his second began on the same tundra, but this time he threw for two touchdowns and came away a 30-10 winner.

"It was emotional," Cousins told ESPN through a halting voice after the game. "Coming to this stadium three years ago, tearing my Achilles here, it's been a tough three years. I was just grateful for the opportunity to play here today and grateful for my teammates and what they did today to make this outcome possible."

Through all of these twists and turns, Cousins has gotten paid . He's totaled $333 million in career earnings , which places him fourth all-time in NFL history, behind Matthew Stafford, Aaron Rodgers and Dak Prescott, and just a tiny slice ahead of Tom Brady. Not bad for a guy who was drafted as a break-glass-in-case-of-emergency backup and has mostly been treated as such ever since.

So what now for Cousins? Well, he's joining a fearsome defensive unit; he basically needs to exhibit just baseline competence and the Vikings will be in the postseason hunt. Minnesota has the 10th-toughest schedule remaining, per Tankathon , but that's largely because the Vikings still need to close out the tough NFC North — and they have the easiest schedule of any of their division opponents.

Right this moment, Minnesota's defense is Super Bowl-caliber. That's why the Vikings acquired Cousins, whom they perceive as an upgrade over Kyler Murray, Carson Wentz or any other potential signal-caller. J.J. McCarthy, performing adequately in New York, is obviously no longer an option.

So after all this, it'd be some kind of peculiar narrative perfection if Cousins manages to win a Super Bowl at last. Stranger things have happened, quite often to Cousins himself.

articles.title: "God-awful" is how Rob Gronkowski describes Tommy DeVito’s Patriots performance, leaving little room for excuses
articles.summary: Tommy DeVito's chance to prove himself as Drake Maye's backup could hardly have gone worse.
articles.body: Tommy DeVito's chance to prove himself as Drake Maye's backup could hardly have gone worse. The New England Patriots suffered a 35-10 defeat against the Detroit Lions, and the quarterback's struggles after replacing the injured Maye only added to the team's problems. DeVito managed just 81 passing yards, threw an interception and took four sacks. His display caught the attention of former Patriots star Rob Gronkowski, who offered a particularly harsh assessment of the NFL on FOX. Gronkowski made little effort to soften his words, raising fresh questions about New England's quarterback depth.Rob Gronkowski doesn't hold back on Tommy DeVito's Patriots performanceGronkowski said he had an early feeling that New England's offense would struggle once Maye left the game. What followed only strengthened that impression. DeVito completed 12 of 24 passes for 81 yards, with one touchdown and one interception. The numbers told a difficult story, but Gronkowski's reaction made clear that he was concerned about more than the final statistics.“Once Drake May went down, I saw their first drive,” Gronkowski said. “I texted my buddy, and I said, ‘This New England Patriots offense is only going to have 75 yards of offense for the rest of the game.’ That was horrendous. It was god-awful watching him play.”The former tight end also questioned whether DeVito looked ready to handle the responsibility. He acknowledged that the quarterback had not necessarily expected to enter the game, but felt the lack of control was obvious.“No weapons at all,” he added. “The quarterback just wasn’t doing what he needed to do. I could just tell, like Fernando, he looks like he belongs. Tommy DeVito just didn’t look like he belonged out there. He didn’t have a grasp on the situation. Like he wasn’t prepared that he was going to go into the game, which I understand.”That comparison is significant. Gronkowski was not simply asking DeVito to match Maye's production. He wanted to see a backup who could settle the offense, make sensible decisions and give the Patriots a chance to compete. Instead, New England struggled to find any rhythm.Drake Maye's injury makes Patriots' Quarterback situation more complicatedThe criticism carries more weight because Maye's availability is now a major concern. The young quarterback suffered an ankle injury against Detroit, and reports have raised fears that the damage could keep him out for an extended period, potentially even the rest of the season. Nothing about his recovery timeline is settled yet.That uncertainty leaves New England with an uncomfortable decision. DeVito is currently in line for an opportunity if Maye cannot return, but his performance has hardly made the coaching staff's job easier.The Patriots dropped to 5-5 with the defeat and now have their bye week to review what went wrong. Head coach Mike Vrabel has expressed confidence in DeVito and rookie Behren Morton, while acknowledging that the backup needs to improve after his outing.There is also a possibility that New England looks outside the building. NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported that the Patriots are expected to explore quarterback options during the break. Jimmy Garoppolo has emerged as a potential name, although no move has been confirmed.For DeVito, the next few days matter. He has time to study the film and work on his mistakes, but the bigger issue is whether the Patriots can afford to wait for him to find his footing with Maye's status uncertain.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Ahead of the holiday season, the popular podcast host Kylie Kelce reflects on how the family prepares for the holiday season.Jason Kelce’s wife Kylie Kelce opens up about how their family gears up for the holiday season and what it is like with four daughtersA few hours ago, in an interview with TODAY, the Not Gonna Lie podcast host Kylie Kelce opened up about it as she said, “My sister is in the kitchen, and if my mother-in-law Donna (Kelce) is there, she’ll help chop vegetables or read books to the girls…Keeping the kids occupied is just as important to getting the meal finished.”Jason Kelce’s wife Kylie Kelce added, “If I tell you dinner is at 4, we might sit down by 6:30. articles.title: Jason Kelce challenges NFL celebration culture after Aidan Hutchinson’s ACL tear brings past injuries back into focus
articles.summary: Jason Kelce believes NFL teams should teach players safer ways to celebrate after Detroit Lions star Aidan Hutchinson suffered a torn ACL during a sack
articles.body: Jason Kelce believes NFL teams should teach players safer ways to celebrate after Detroit Lions star Aidan Hutchinson suffered a torn ACL during a sack celebration against the New England Patriots. The injury has raised fresh questions about players putting themselves at risk after big moments. Speaking on ESPN’s Monday Night Countdown, Kelce suggested that coaches should step in and make players aware of the dangers of certain celebrations.Jason Kelce calls for changes to NFL celebrations after Aidan Hutchinson’s ACL injuryKelce shared his thoughts after Hutchinson went down during Detroit’s game against New England in Munich on Sunday, November 15. The defensive end had just brought down Patriots quarterback Drake Maye for a sack when he jumped into the air to celebrate. However, his landing went badly, and he immediately fell to the ground while holding his right knee.Hutchinson was taken off the field for medical attention and did not return to the game. Further tests confirmed that he had torn his ACL, ending his 2026 season. For Kelce, the incident was another example of how a celebration can turn into a serious injury.The former Philadelphia Eagles center pointed to several similar incidents from previous years and said teams should take a closer look at how players celebrate.“I think there’s enough evidence out there now,” Kelce said on the ESPN show.He also brought up former Detroit Lions linebacker Stephen Tulloch, who tore his ACL while celebrating a sack in 2014. Kelce mentioned Lamarr Houston, who suffered the same injury during that season, along with former Arizona Cardinals kicker Bill Gramatica, who also injured his ACL after jumping during a celebration in 2001.“There’s enough evidence now, where, maybe we should be coaching these guys. We should be coaching celebrations differently,” Kelce added. “You hate to see something like this happen, especially to a guy who is impactful and is great as a player as he is.”Kelce also recalled the discussion around Hutchinson’s Cristiano Ronaldo-inspired “SIUUUU” celebration in September. The move involves jumping and landing, making it look similar to the celebration that led to Tulloch’s injury years earlier.Jason McCourty disagrees with Jason Kelce’s suggestion to regulate player celebrationsHowever, not everyone on the ESPN panel agreed with Kelce. Former New England Patriots defensive back Jason McCourty questioned whether coaches could realistically control how players react after making a big play.McCourty explained that jumping is already a normal part of football training, so banning players from leaving their feet during celebrations would be difficult to enforce. He also pointed out that players cannot always predict how they will react in an emotional moment.“I hear what you’re saying, but this is a box jump,” McCourty said. “This is what guys do during the offseason, when they’re doing 50 box jumps, and you’re completely OK.“I think it’s hard to coach celebrations. I don’t know how I’m going to react if I get a pick-six. And coaches, if they say, ‘Guys, you’re not allowed to leave our feet in celebration.’ What are you going to do as a coach? Are you going to fine them? To me, I understand what you’re saying, and you hate to see the injury; I just can’t see us trying to regulate.”Kelce did not push the argument much further after hearing McCourty’s response, but the discussion highlighted a problem that has affected athletes across different sports.Former New York Mets pitcher Edwin Diaz also suffered a serious knee injury while celebrating with his teammates after a game at the 2023 World Baseball Classic. Similarly, Gramatica’s 2001 injury and Tulloch’s 2014 ACL tear remain examples of celebrations going wrong.Not every serious injury happens during a celebration, either. San Francisco 49ers linebacker Dre Greenlaw tore his ACL while running onto the field during Super Bowl LVIII in 2024, showing that injuries can happen even during routine movements.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: Stefon Diggs might have expected some awkwardness with Cardi B's former husband, Offset, but the rapper is making it clear that he has no plans of turning their situation into a personal feud. The Migos rapper recently sat down with Tony Yayo and Uncle Murda on The Real Report, where the conversation eventually turned to Cardi B and her relationship with the NFL star. articles.title: "Enough with the Kelces": Jason Kelce's saxophone performance sparks fresh NFL fan backlash

articles.body: Jason Kelce traded the football field for a musical performance on Monday night, but his latest appearance has not exactly won over everyone. Insufferable f***."The criticism also extended beyond the saxophone performance, with some fans expressing frustration over the constant attention surrounding the Kelce family."I've never been so sick of seeing someone. articles.title: NFL flexes injury-riddled Patriots out of SNF in Week 12, swaps in Raiders and Fernando Mendoza
articles.summary: This year's No. 1 overall pick will get his first primetime game.
articles.body:
The NFL announced Tuesday that it would switch to the Week 12 schedule. Originally, the New England Patriots were scheduled to face the Los Angeles Chargers on "Sunday Night Football."

Now, the league updated the schedule and moved three games around. The Patriots and Chargers will kick off at 4:05 p.m. ET, which bumps the Jacksonville Jaguars and Tennessee Titans' AFC South divisional battle to 1 p.m. ET.

The new "Sunday Night Football" matchup will see the Las Vegas Raiders go on the road to take on the Cleveland Browns.

No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza made his NFL debut last week against the Seattle Seahawks. Las Vegas lost and fell to 4-6. Mendoza finished with 143 passing yards passing, no turnovers and a rushing TD.

If he avoids injury against the Denver Broncos in Week 11, Mendoza would be in line for his first primetime start against the Browns.

Cleveland is 6-4 and third in the AFC North. Quarterback Deshaun Watson leads the league in fourth-quarter comeback wins. So while Browns games may not have been the most exciting early on, they tend to have fireworks late.

New England and Los Angeles looked like a blockbuster matchup when the schedule dropped this offseason. After 10 weeks, though, the Patriots are preparing to be without quarterback Drake Maye for the foreseeable future after he suffered an injury in last week's loss to the Detroit Lions.

The Chargers picked up a big win Monday night against the Baltimore Ravens, but it was their first win of the year, and they are now 1-8.

For now, the league puts the No. 1 pick in primetime as Las Vegas gears up to take on the Broncos this week. Cleveland is on bye and should be well rested when the Browns host the Raiders the following week.

articles.body: Travis Kelce’s commitment to empowering Kansas City youth is once again taking centermost stage. This time, students from Operation Breakthrough’s Ignition Lab, powered by Kelce’s 87 & Running Foundation, will showcase their creative work at Strawberry Swing Indie Craft Fair’s 16th Annual Holiday Swing.The two-day holiday event will bring together 100 independent artists, small businesses, and local makers under one roof. It will take place on November 21 and 22, 2026, at Union Station’s Haverty Family Yards in Kansas City, Missouri. Visitors can attend the family-friendly event for free from 10:00 AM to 6:00 PM on both days.Travis Kelce backed Ignition Lab students join Strawberry Swing holiday marketStrawberry Swing’s Holiday Market is returning to Union Station, where the event originally began. Organized by Strawberry Swing Indie Craft Fair, the gathering celebrates independent artists and handmade products while encouraging visitors to support small businesses and local makers.The family-friendly event will feature curated local and regional vendors, handmade holiday gifts, festive food and drinks, and holiday music. The European-inspired open-air market will give visitors an opportunity to discover unique products and meet the makers behind them.The participation of Operation Breakthrough’s Ignition Lab adds a community-focused dimension to this year’s celebration, giving young Kansas City creatives an opportunity to showcase their work beyond their usual learning environment. Isn’t this exactly what Travis Kelce loves? More creative opportunities for youth.Travis Kelce’s 87 & Running Foundation supports Ignition LabTravis Kelce founded 87 & Running in 2015 to empower underserved youth through mentorship, resources, and opportunities in education, business, athletics, STEM, and the arts. His partnership with Operation Breakthrough speaks volumes about the foundation’s commitment to extending opportunities for young people.In summer of 2020, Kelce made a massive $500,000 donation to purchase a building adjacent to the Operation Breakthrough’s facility, which was transformed into the Ignition Lab. The facility provides teenagers with a dedicated space to explore careers, develop practical skills, and gain real-world experience.“The vision is to give them [teenagers] a safe haven where they can continue to find role models, discover interests and develop skills once they age out of OB [Operation Breakthrough]’s after-school program.I’m so excited to be purchasing a building adjacent to OB’s MakerCity that will be the future home of ‘The Ignition Lab, powered by 87 & Running,’” Travis Kelce said via Operation Breakthrough’s official website.Ignition Lab students showcase their creative talentOperation Breakthrough launched the Ignition Lab in 2021, with support from Travis Kelce’s 87 & Running Foundation.The workforce development initiative provides teenagers aged 14 to 18 with several opportunities to explore career paths through hands-on experiences, creative projects, mentorship, and skill development.Students gain massive exposure to fields such as computer technology, graphic design, mechatronics, construction, product design, automotive engineering, culinary arts, and digital media. The program aims to help them develop practical skills and prepare for employment, entrepreneurship, or higher education.According to a December 2024 KCTV5 report, the Ignition Lab served approximately 400 high school students in Kansas City. By then, teenagers had completed 300 projects with earnest support from Travis Kelce.“It’s been huge having Travis because it’s almost like he’s become a spokesman for the work that happens here and the impact that it has on teens, and as he’s gotten busier and his world has changed in terms of everything that he’s doing, he still manages to share us with his circle of influence,” Operation Breakthrough CEO Mary Esselman told KCTV5 in 2024.The upcoming Strawberry Swing holiday market will give participating students another opportunity to introduce their creative work to the Kansas City community.Kansas City community celebrates young creativesStrawberry Swing’s 16th Annual Holiday Market will be more than a seasonal shopping destination. articles.title: “He speaks English just fine”: Raiders face backlash over Fernando Mendoza's Spanish-speaking interaction
articles.summary: The Las Vegas Raiders were seemingly trying to make Fernando Mendoza feel at home during his first start as the team's quarterback.
articles.body: The Las Vegas Raiders were seemingly trying to make Fernando Mendoza feel at home during his first start as the team's quarterback. However, a small gesture from his teammates and coaches has unexpectedly turned into a talking point among NFL fans.During Sunday's Week 10 matchup against the Seattle Seahawks, Raiders players and coaches were caught speaking Spanish to Mendoza on the sidelines. The NFL later shared a compilation of the interactions in its Week 10 Mic'd Up video, highlighting how the team used Spanish phrases while communicating with the rookie.Fernando Mendoza's Spanish-speaking moment doesn't sit well with some fansOne of the most noticeable moments came when teammate Aidan O'Connell was heard telling Mendoza, "Respira," which means "breathe" in Spanish. Another moment featured the words "Tranquilo. Congratulations," as the team celebrated with the young quarterback.The NFL shared the clip with the caption, "Raiders coaches and players spoke Spanish to Fernando Mendoza during his first start," seemingly highlighting the team's effort to connect with the rookie and acknowledge his Cuban heritage.However, not everyone was impressed by the gesture.The NFL's post quickly attracted attention, with some fans questioning why the Raiders were making a point of speaking Spanish to Mendoza when English is reportedly the language he is more comfortable using.Sports columnist Armando Salguero also weighed in, questioning the purpose of the gesture. In a post on X, he wrote that Mendoza speaks English and is actually more comfortable speaking English than Spanish.He then questioned whether the moment was anything more than virtue signaling. That criticism found support among some NFL fans, who felt the interaction looked forced rather than natural.One fan commented, "This is so weird. It’s almost insulting. lol"Another wrote, "As a hispanic American born here whose last name is like Mendoza, I hate when people speak Spanish to me or ask me to eat a taco. It's extremly patronizing."Mendoza's Cuban heritage adds another layer to the discussionMendoza's background is an important part of why the moment attracted so much attention. The rookie quarterback is of Cuban descent and made history after becoming the first player of Cuban descent to be selected No. 1 overall in the NFL Draft.The Raiders' gesture appeared to acknowledge that heritage, but the discussion has also raised questions about the difference between celebrating someone's cultural background and making assumptions about their language preferences.Mendoza's first start was already a significant moment for the franchise. He completed 17 of 29 passes for 143 yards and recorded his first NFL touchdown on a 10-yard rushing play. However, the Raiders ultimately fell 21-13 to the Seahawks.While some fans found the Spanish exchanges awkward, others saw them as a harmless attempt by teammates to support their rookie quarterback. Either way, what was meant to be a small moment of encouragement has turned into a much bigger NFL conversation.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: “I wake up tired”: Tom Brady shares a vulnerable message revealing the reality behind his success
articles.summary: Tom Brady might have walked away from the NFL, but his competitive mindset clearly hasn't gone anywhere.
articles.body: Tom Brady might have walked away from the NFL, but his competitive mindset clearly hasn't gone anywhere. The seven-time Super Bowl champion recently shared a candid message about discipline, consistency and pushing through exhaustion, reminding everyone that success isn't always about talent or motivation. Sometimes, it's simply about showing up when you least feel like it.Tom Brady gets brutally honest about the difficult days behind his legendary NFL successBrady took to his Instagram Story to share a lengthy message that he continues to live by. One particular line immediately stood out: "I wake up tired and still outwork people who feel fine."The former New England Patriots and Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback didn't stop there. He went on to explain why waiting for motivation can sometimes hold people back from achieving their goals."Some days, the difference isn't talent. It's the decision to keep showing up anyway," Brady wrote.He also admitted that he had stopped waiting to feel ready because he realized that progress is often built on the days when people would rather stay in bed.The NFL legend's message focused heavily on the importance of keeping promises to yourself, even when circumstances aren't ideal. According to Brady, the people who achieve the results everyone admires aren't necessarily those who always feel motivated. Instead, they are the ones who continue working when things become inconvenient, uncomfortable and exhausting.He further explained that the body might ask for comfort and the mind might ask for a break, but having a purpose bigger than your excuses can keep you moving forward."And over time, that consistency becomes the reason you end up where others never do," he added.It is a message that sounds particularly familiar coming from someone who spent more than two decades competing at the highest level of professional football.The mentality that helped Tom Brady build an NFL dynastyBrady's career is perhaps one of the biggest examples of what long-term discipline can accomplish in professional sports.Across 23 NFL seasons, the quarterback won seven Super Bowl championships, six with the New England Patriots and another with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.He built his legacy through years of preparation, attention to detail and an almost unmatched commitment to staying competitive. Even as younger quarterbacks entered the league, Brady continued to find ways to perform at an elite level.His final NFL season came in 2022, but retirement hasn't necessarily meant leaving that competitive mindset behind. Brady has since taken on a new role as an NFL analyst for FOX Sports while remaining involved in several business ventures. Although his days of preparing for NFL defenses are over, his latest message suggests that the habits associated with his football career remain a major part of his everyday life.For a player who spent 23 seasons chasing greatness, the message feels particularly fitting. Brady might no longer be taking snaps on Sundays, but if his latest words are anything to go by, the seven-time Super Bowl champion still approaches life with the same mentality that helped make him one of football's greatest players.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Tom Brady steals the spotlight in Bill Belichick’s Travis Burgess discussion as UNC faces a crucial quarterback decision
articles.summary: Bill Belichick has reminded everyone that a young quarterback does not need years of experience to succeed, using Tom Brady’s early career to make his
articles.body: Bill Belichick has reminded everyone that a young quarterback does not need years of experience to succeed, using Tom Brady’s early career to make his point as North Carolina faces a possible change under center. With Billy Edwards Jr. dealing with an injury, freshman Travis Burgess could get his first college start against Virginia on November 21. Belichick believes the opportunity matters more than a player’s experience.Bill Belichick uses Tom Brady’s rise to explain Travis Burgess’ opportunity at UNCNorth Carolina’s quarterback situation changed during its 16-14 loss to Louisville on November 14. Edwards, who had started the team’s first 10 games, left after suffering an upper-body injury in the third quarter. Belichick then turned to Burgess, a true freshman who was making his first appearance in college football.The young quarterback completed six of his 11 passes for 59 yards and added 35 yards on eight carries. He also had a chance to lead a late comeback, but his final pass was intercepted after it bounced off wide receiver Jordan Shipp.Now, with UNC preparing for its next game against Virginia, Belichick is keeping Edwards’ status open. During his Monday press conference, he said the quarterback’s availability would be assessed day by day.When asked whether Burgess had enough experience to handle the job, Belichick brought up a quarterback whose early career followed a very different path from his later success. He did not mention Tom Brady by name, but the description clearly pointed toward the former New England Patriots star.According to Michael McCleary of The News & Observer, Belichick reminded reporters that he had won a Super Bowl with a quarterback who had once been a fourth-string player at Michigan. That player was Brady, who was also buried on New England’s depth chart when he arrived in 2000.After Drew Bledsoe suffered an injury during the 2001 season, Brady got his chance to start. He helped the Patriots win Super Bowl XXXVI against the St. Louis Rams, with Belichick leading the team. When asked about the quarterback’s performance, Belichick added, “And he played pretty good.”The coach was not saying Burgess would become another Brady. Instead, he wanted to make clear that a lack of experience does not automatically mean a quarterback cannot get the job done.Bill Belichick explains what Travis Burgess must handle if Billy Edwards Jr. remains outBelichick also spoke about the biggest challenge Burgess could face if he starts against Virginia. Practicing without contact is very different from playing when defenders are trying to reach the quarterback.As backups wear red non-contact jerseys during practice, they can throw without worrying about being hit. Belichick explained the difference in simple terms.“It’s easy to go back there and chuck it on the mound, and nobody’s coming at you,” he said. “You throw 100 miles an hour, let it go. A little bit different when they’re running at you.”The coach does not expect a major change to the offense if Burgess plays. He may add a few plays or use different formations, but the overall plan will remain familiar. Edwards had more practice time with the Louisville game plan, so Burgess has not worked through every play.North Carolina also uses virtual reality sessions to help its quarterbacks prepare. The system allows them to practise reading defensive coverage, calling plays and following the right footwork before facing an opponent.The Tar Heels are 5-5 and need one more win to become eligible for a bowl game. They have two regular-season games left, starting with Virginia on November 21, followed by NC State.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
