articles.title: Royals add three players to 40-man roster ahead of deadline
articles.summary: The two guys you expected made it, but there was one surprise!
articles.body:
The Royals announced earlier today, ahead of the deadline to protect players from the Rule-5 Draft (which may or may not occur, as it is scheduled for after the MLB Lockout is expected to begin), that they had added three players to the 40-man roster.

Carson Roccaforte is considered the Royals' 17th-best prospect by MLB Pipeline after slashing .257/.338/.519/.857 with 35 home runs and 32 steals last year while splitting time between Northwest Arkansas and Omaha. He is widely expected to compete for an outfield job with the Royals during Spring Training. He's not higher on the Royals' prospect lists because he also struck out 29.1% of the time last year. However, if he can offer a defensive upgrade over the declining Kyle Isbel and pop 20 home runs a year, he could be a valuable member of the roster at the major league minimum.

Lucas Braun was acquired in the Lane Thomas trade last year (the one that was dulled by the inclusion of Bailey Falter for salary relief). Braun is considered the Royals' 16th-best prospect by MLB Pipeline. Funnily enough, he comes in at 27th to Roccaforte's 26th per FanGraphs . Braun had pitched to a 3.92 ERA for Atlanta's AAA affiliate before the trade, but fell to a 5.73 ERA once he joined Omaha's staff. Interestingly, he struck out about 50% more hitters with the Royals, but he gave up significantly more home runs, too. If he could keep the strikeouts but ditch the home runs, he could become a very valuable prospect for the Royals.

Nick Mears was acquired by KC last off-season in the Angel Zerpa trade. He was expected to help solidify the middle of the bullpen, but instead he pitched to a 5.19 ERA in his first 21 appearances before missing the rest of the season with an injury. He was a non-tender candidate and hits the market just a few days ahead of the deadline to tender contract offers to those on the team without guaranteed deals for 2027.

If you've been keeping track at home until today, you might recall that the Royals had two open roster spots and shouldn't have needed to waive Mears to fit their two additions. However, they made a trade a few hours prior to the deadline that resulted in filling another roster spot.

Angel Bastardo was considered the Red Sox 18th-best prospect by FanGraphs prior to the trade and is now considered the Royals' 20th-best prospect by MLB Pipeline. He has a fastball that can reach 95-97, but FanGraphs reports that it plays poorly because his release slot gives it a poor shape. He has an excellent changeup, but can struggle to command his breaking pitches.

Still, as you can see from the above summary, all of his pitches can generate both chase and whiffs. He struck out more than 12 batters per 9 innings last year. If he can harness just a bit more command, he could turn into a weapon out of the bullpen. He has already been taken in a Rule 5 draft before, and the Red Sox may have feared losing him a second time but still been unwilling to protect him. Trading him to the Royals for a 27-year-old infielder who has not yet reached the big leagues may have seemed the better of two evils.

Jack Pineda absolutely demolished AA pitching as a 26-year-old this year, and he even hit well for Omaha, slashing a combined .351/.413/.530/.944 between the two levels. Maybe it was a breakout for a late bloomer, but history is littered with far more CJ Alexanders than Whit Merrifields.

articles.title: Tuesday Miami Dolphins Thoughts With The Earl
articles.summary: If you were waiting for the opportune moment… that was it.
articles.body:
This game really depends upon your outlook for the season. If you are a "get the first draft pick at all costs" person, then you like this outcome. If you want to see a win and positive development, this was a horrible outcome. It was another of the "close, but no cigar" games the Dolphins have played this season. Here's what I saw.

In previous games, there was a tradeoff between the offense and defense over which would show up. In this game, the offense was expected to be worse than the defense, with a backup QB getting his first-ever NFL action. However, the Dolphins still couldn't go a game without some form of tradeoff. In this matchup, it was a tradeoff between the pass defense and the run defense. The Dolphins allowed a completion percentage over 70% and had a run defense that allowed less than 4 yards per carry. The pass defense had its best performance of the season. They held Danny Dimes to 50% completion and a 4.9 YPA average. They picked him off twice, one of which was returned for a TD. They allowed a passing TD and a couple of big plays but were solid in coverage. In a shock to everyone, the Dolphins allowed more rushing yards to TE Tyler Warren (3) than receiving yards (1). Warren was held without a catch until the 4th quarter and was a complete non-factor.

Unfortunately, while the Dolphins pass defense stepped up covering the one receiving threat the Colts had, the run defense couldn't stop the other threat the Colts posed. The Colts rushed for 172 yards on 34 carries, 106 of those yards coming in the 1st half on 19 carries. That's a 5.6 YPA allowed. They improved a little in the second half, allowing 66 yards on 15 carries and a 4.4 YPA. But on the final drive, they allowed 12 yards on 2 carries that finished off the game. Just once, the team needs a complete performance on both sides of the ball. Now they need a complete performance on both sides of the ball. I will give them some due credit. They limited the Colts to 17 offensive points and were hamstrung by a limited offense, but the run defense was the backbreaker in this game. With the injuries mounting on the DL, I don't know how they can fix it.

We'll get to the obvious problem in a moment. Bradley Pinion had 3 punts for 134 yards, with a 55-yarder. That's an average of 44.7 overall and 39.5 on the other two punts. Indy's punter had 6 for 290, averaging 48.3. The league average is 47.5. Miami still allowed too many yards in the kick return game. They had the 15-yard penalty on Louis, though I won't complain about penalties since the total was lopsided in Miami's favor and that penalty was ultimately inconsequential. It is still unacceptable, though.

I said on Friday that the Dolphins simply aren't good enough to win without winning in the margins. This is a young team working to find its identity. They come to work every day and put it all on the line every game. This isn't the 2024 or 2025 Dolphins with players obviously checking out and Tua laughing on the sideline or Hill taking himself out of a game. This is a bad team playing like they are trying to get the top seed in the AFC. When the kicker, the second oldest player on the team, shanks not one, but two FGs and misses a PAT as the icing on the cake, that is a level of terrible that cannot be measured. After I watched the game and went to bed thinking of all I planned to say about how he cannot remain on the team if the coaches wanna keep the locker room, the Dolphins made my job easier and waived him on Monday. So that is a non-issue now.

And I've seen the tweets about how the misses keep the tank alive and all that. But I cannot stress enough how not only is tanking a bad idea in general, but you really only tank for a QB, and the 2027 QB class is buns. They are bad. It's an elevated class due to absences and wouldn't be considered top prospects in a class like 2018 or 2020. I would love for the Dolphins to get Jeremiah Smith as much as any other fan. But this team is NOT trying to lose. They aren't playing like they are trying to lose. They are talent deficient, but they aren't tanking. So when you play as hard as they do and the veteran kicker can't do the basic requirement of putting the ball through the uprights, then a message needs to be sent, and it was.

Kyle McCord's play will be dissected by many others, so I don't want to get deep into it. I thought he played ok. I thought he played like a player getting his first NFL snaps. His performance isn't worth getting worked up over one way or another. I said in Friday's post that a healthy Willis wins this game by 2 scores, and I still believe it. But McCord played well enough for the Dolphins to get a win against another equally terrible team and was let down. The next step will be to see what, if any, level of improvements can be made.

The run game has disappeared, and it probably won't come back for a while. I tried to watch to see how much Indy loaded the box, but I didn't truly keep track. Indy is a bad team, but Miami will face some good teams coming up; teams with solid to great defenses. My guess is they will load the box and force McCord to beat them. Having Meyer in there instead of Brewer hurt as well, but the OL can only do so much. The good news for the RBs is they were involved in the passing game. All three RBs were targeted 9 times with 8 catches for 62 yards, including the 4-yard loss for Kaytron Allen. If the RBs can contribute in the pass game, then the offense can function about as normally as we can expect. Even with the drop-off, Gordon is still on pace for a 1000 yard season.

Caleb Douglas was invisible for most of the game but stepped up late. He will continue to be a force. Washington had the play of the game IMO with the one-handed catch down the sideline. He continues to improve in getting separation and being a factor in the offense. The TD throw was nice also.

The TEs were invisible, and that's a concern. I like Dulcich, and he has potential, but he is playing his way off the roster for 2027.

The passing defense stepped up as I mentioned, and its leaders are two rookies. Michael Taaffe logged his 3rd INT this season, and Chris Johnson got his 2nd in consecutive weeks. It should have been his 3rd in 4 weeks, but that Jets WR fell down and they said Johnson interfered. He was a ballhawk in college, and it is showing up now. There are 17 players in the league with 3 or more INTs and only 7 with more than 3. Taaffe has the instincts to be around the ball a lot. His development going into the rest of this season will be interesting to watch.

Regarding the kicker position, I would not be opposed to the Dolphins adding a young player – an undrafted rookie or second-year player – to fill the position. Vets are what they are, and while they offer some reliability, I'm all for giving a young player a chance to make his mark. They probably won't because, well, they are trying to win games. But if they swing and miss with young players, at least they tried. If they get a hit, that's something they can build on moving forward.

Circling back to the opening paragraph, I am not a fan of losing games for a draft pick. I want the Dolphins to win. This game was frustrating because they had it and gave it away. They lost by the margins and lost the game. Unfortunately, this was the last win on the schedule for a while. Unless McCord magically turns into Tom Brady in the next few games, the Dolphins are looking at 1-16. They host the Jets in 2 weeks, but I don't like that matchup with McCord. They host the hapless Chargers in week 16, and if Willis is back healthy, they'll have a good chance of winning. They have the 8-1 Bills and 7-2 Broncos on the road in 2 of the next 3 games. They get the 7-2 Bears and 6-4 Packers, all battling for playoff seeding and that division title. Perhaps the Bills will lock up home-field advantage by week 17, and the Dolphins will get backups. Otherwise, the outlook is grim. To paraphrase Captain Jack Sparrow: if you were waiting for the opportune moment to get a win… that was it.

We all knew this season wasn't about the wins, but 1-16 is a tough mark for anyone. Even if the Dolphins go 12-5 over the next 2 seasons (they won't), that is still 25-26 over 3 seasons. It's going to be much worse than that. It is going to be a long road back to relevance for this franchise. I'll cover that later on (either this week or next), so stay tuned.

articles.title: Matt Prater Has Chiefs Tryout Amid Harrison Butker's Struggles, Justin Tucker Contract
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs worked out free agent kicker Matt Prater on Tuesday, per the NFL's transaction wire.
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs worked out free agent kicker Matt Prater on Tuesday, per the NFL's transaction wire .

The workout is amid continued struggles for kicker Harrison Butker, who has missed 7-of-19 field goals this season. Kansas City previously signed former Baltimore Ravens kicker Justin Tucker to its practice squad on Oct. 28.

The 42-year-old Prater has kicked for the Atlanta Falcons (2007), Denver Broncos (2007-2013), Detroit Lions (2014-2020), Arizona Cardinals (2021-2024) and Buffalo Bills (2025) over his 19-season career. He fared well for Buffalo in 2025, making 23-of-25 field goals (including playoffs) and 46-of-49 extra points.

Prater also made some clutch kicks, including a 50-yarder as regulation expired in the Bills' eventual 33-30 overtime road loss to the Denver Broncos in the AFC Divisional round.

As for Butker, he's enjoyed great success over the majority of his 10-season tenure in the league and helped the Chiefs win three Super Bowls. However, this season has been tough to say the least.

The 10-year veteran missed 3-of-6 field goals over Weeks 7-9. Despite his struggles and the team's Oct. 28 addition of Tucker on the practice squad, head coach Andy Reid told reporters he was going to "stick with Butker" and that the team would "go from there."

Butker didn't attempt a field goal last Sunday in the team's 35-12 road win over the Atlanta Falcons, but he did make all five of his extra points.

Ultimately, Butker remains the Chiefs' kicker at this moment as the 7-2 squad returns home to face the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday. We'll see if anything arises from Prater's tryout, but Tucker still remains on the practice squad as well.

articles.title: Miami Dolphins sign kicker Daniel Carlson to practice squad
articles.summary: Daniel Carlson, 31, who worked out for the Dolphins last week, was waived by the New Orleans Saints earlier this month after converting 8 of 12 field goals.
articles.body:
The Miami Dolphins will be using their third place-kicker of the 2026 NFL season Sunday when they play at the Buffalo Bills .

Daniel Carlson was signed to the team's practice squad on Tuesday, one day after the Dolphins waived Zane Gonzalez , whose missed two field goals and extra-point led to the 24-22 loss to the Indianapolis Colts . Gonzalez had replaced the struggling Riley Patterson last month.

Carlson, 31, who worked out for the team last week, was waived by the New Orleans Saints earlier this month after converting 8 of 12 field goals. The bulk of his career was with the Raiders , but Carlson's field goal accuracy had declined over his final two seasons with Las Vegas, dropping to 81.5% in 2025.

He has appeared in 136 career games in nine seasons with Minnesota (2018), Oakland/Las Vegas (2018-25) and New Orleans (2026). He has converted 233-of-271 career field goal attempts (86.0 percent), along with 260-of-273 extra points (95.2 percent).

Carlson was named a first-team All-Pro in 2022 and received second-team All-Pro honors in 2021. He entered the NFL as a fifth-round selection (167th overall) by Minnesota in the 2018 NFL Draft after playing at Auburn where he appeared in 53 career games and converted 92-of-114 field goal attempts (80.7%) - and was a perfect 198-of-198 on PATs.

articles.title: Rex Ryan’s Accuser Takes Brutal Five-Word Shot In Furious 911 Call
articles.summary: Rex Ryan’s red pickup truck got a memorable description in a newly released 911 call. Nashville attorney Michael Holland was […]
articles.body:
Rex Ryan 's red pickup truck got a memorable description in a newly released 911 call. Nashville attorney Michael Holland was on the phone with a dispatcher after he says the former NFL coach drove over his and his wife's feet on Broadway. Holland wanted Ryan arrested, and when the dispatcher asked what the truck looked like, he made sure to get in a dig about its oversized wheels.

The call came shortly before midnight on November 5. Ryan, who coached the New York Jets and Buffalo Bills before joining ESPN, later turned himself in and faces six misdemeanor charges.

Michael Holland Demands Rex Ryan's Arrest In 911 Call

In audio obtained by the New York Post, Holland told the dispatcher that he and his wife had been crossing Broadway when the truck hit them. "I just got, literally, my wife and I both got ran over by some [expletive] on [expletive] Broadway and I want to turn him in," Holland said.

The attorney kept answering the dispatcher's questions, but he made clear what he wanted police to do. "He [expletive] needs to be arrested," he said. Holland also called Ryan "just a d-khead" who "needs to not be driving."

Holland told the dispatcher the couple didn't need an ambulance, though he said it "[expletive] hurt." Nashville police later described their injuries as minor.

The Caller Takes A Shot At Ryan's Pickup Truck

ALERT: Former NFL head coach Rex Ryan was caught in an alleged hit-and-run partially because of his vanity license plate that says "HIT QBS." pic.twitter.com/F0alWe7DNl — E X X ➠A L E R T S (@ExxAlerts) November 13, 2026

ALERT: Former NFL head coach Rex Ryan was caught in an alleged hit-and-run partially because of his vanity license plate that says "HIT QBS." pic.twitter.com/F0alWe7DNl

E X X ➠A L E R T S (@ExxAlerts) November 13, 2026

When the dispatcher asked Holland to describe the vehicle, he gave them the color, the size and his own take on the wheels. "A big red pickup truck with oversized wheels that said small p-nis," he replied.

Holland also gave the dispatcher a more specific detail. The truck had a New York vanity plate that reportedly read "HIT QBS," an apparent nod to Ryan's years coaching NFL defenses. Police said the plate was registered to Ryan. Investigators also said the couple photographed the truck and its driver after the alleged incident.

The Metropolitan Nashville Police Department said the couple was crossing Broadway near Fourth Avenue with a walk signal when Ryan allegedly turned right. Authorities allege that the truck ran over both pedestrians' feet and made contact with one person's leg before continuing down Broadway.

According to police, the couple caught up to the truck at another red light and confronted Ryan. Investigators said he got out, argued with them and then drove away without giving them his information or offering aid. Police also reportedly obtained surveillance footage of the incident.

Rex Ryan Surrenders And Faces Six Misdemeanor Charges

Ryan turned himself in on November 11 after learning that warrants had been issued for his arrest. He faces two counts of leaving the scene of an accident, two counts of failing to provide information or render aid and two counts of failing to obey a traffic control signal.

A judicial commissioner set bond at $6,000, and Ryan was released under non-financial pretrial conditions. He is scheduled to appear in court on December 18.

Ryan's attorney previously said the former coach surrendered as soon as he learned about the warrants and intended to cooperate as the case moved forward.

Ryan Returns To ESPN Days After His Arrest

🚨Days after his Nashville arrest for running over the feet of two pedestrians with his truck, Rex Ryan is pushing publicly for a job with the Dallas #Cowboys . Per NBC Sports pic.twitter.com/38eNgETnCC — NFL Rumors (@nflrums) November 17, 2026

🚨Days after his Nashville arrest for running over the feet of two pedestrians with his truck, Rex Ryan is pushing publicly for a job with the Dallas #Cowboys . Per NBC Sports pic.twitter.com/38eNgETnCC

Ryan was back on ESPN's "NFL Sunday Countdown" days after turning himself in. He appeared on the network's morning programming again on Monday. The Nashville incident did not come up in his remarks during either appearance.

ESPN previously said it was aware of the situation and remained in contact with Ryan, who joined the network in 2017 after his NFL coaching career.

articles.title: New York Jets insider picks out ‘name to watch’ to replace Aaron Glenn who is already coaching NFL team
articles.summary: New York Jets head coach Aaron Glenn is widely expected to be replaced in the offseason, after another disappointing campaign. Aaron Glenn’s overall record a...
articles.body:
New York Jets head coach Aaron Glenn is widely expected to be replaced in the offseason, after another disappointing campaign.

Aaron Glenn's overall record as the New York Jets head coach is an awful 5-22 across two seasons.

After going 3-14 last season, the Jets have fallen to 2-8 this season. And they are mired in a five-game losing streak.

Speculation is already starting up around possible replacements, with another reboot expected to be required.

Jets insider Frank Cimini claims that Minnesota Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell is an interesting name to watch.

Cimini told the Jets Collective that there is a strong relationship between O'Connell and Jets general manager Darren Mougey.

He said: "The name I would watch for is KOC, Kevin O'Connell. I was just talking to a couple of people in the league today, and they said they could see [Darren] Mougey giving up a high draft pick for Kevin O'Connell.

"They went to college together; they have maintained a relationship. If something falls apart there in Minnesota, if they collapse down the stretch, or if they decide that they want to elevate [Brian] Flores instead of losing him to another team, maybe they make that move."

Kevin O'Connell's Minnesota Vikings are 7-2 and heading for the playoffs. It is unlikely the NFC North team wants to part with him – but Cimini does lay out a couple of scenarios, a possible postseason collapse or a decision to promote their defensive coordinator.

O'Connell is in his first head coaching job with the Vikings after being hired in 2022.

Aaron Glenn spoke of determination to turn Jets around

At the start of November, Aaron Glenn pledged that his full focus was on improving the New York Jets.

When asked about his job, he responded: "There's so much that I think about when it comes to us improving each week that [it] doesn't really come across my mind, to be honest with you.

"I understand how this league is, I understand about what this business is about, but my first job each week is improving this team and that's the only thing that I think about."

The Jets have lost both subsequent games, putting him under even more pressure. Meanwhile, Kevin O'Connell's Vikings have solved their quarterback problem by trading for Kirk Cousins, and are trending upwards.

articles.title: What Tom Brady gained after leaving the NFL: Inside his broadcasting fortune, business empire and changing priorities
articles.summary: Tom Brady now earns more for talking about football than he did for playing it in all but one NFL season.
articles.body: Tom Brady now earns more for talking about football than he did for playing it in all but one NFL season. His Fox contract is reported at 10 years and $375 million, or about $37.5 million a year. On top of that come a roughly five percent stake in the Las Vegas Raiders, stakes in several other teams, and a wellness brand, an apparel line and a production company. Brady turned 49 in August. He is a broadcaster, an owner and an investor at once, and that mix comes with strict rules.The Fox deal is the biggest piece of Tom Brady's new incomeAndrew Marchand first reported the terms in 2022, and the number stunned the industry. It was roughly double what Tony Romo earns at CBS. Marchand later reported that the contract includes stock options, so with Fox performing well, the final value could pass $375 million.The start was bumpy. Brady has said he cringed while watching his early broadcasts. Reviews in his first season were mixed, and Fox shifted Greg Olsen to its second team.Things look better now. Fox saw a 6 percent rise in NFL viewership for the 2025-26 regular season, with 18.7 million viewers per game. That was the network's second-best average since records began in 1988. Brady can't claim all of it, but Fortune wrote that his second season brought clear improvement. At Fox's May upfront presentation he drew big laughs next to Rob Gronkowski and Erin Andrews. He is now in his third season beside Kevin Burkhardt.In early November he went back to Gillette Stadium for the first time as a broadcaster, calling the Patriots and Packers. Brady himself had described the trip as emotional. Patriots quarterback Drake Maye talked about the impact of Brady calling the game.Ownership and outside ventures are changing his prioritiesThe Raiders stake is where the rules get tight. NFL owners voted 32 to 0 in October 2024 to approve Brady as a minority owner of roughly five percent. As part of that, Front Office Sports reports, he cannot criticize teams or referees on air, enter team facilities or attend practices. A columnist at that outlet has argued he may leave the booth well before the contract ends to focus on ownership. His agent, Don Yee, said in January 2025 that Brady intends to finish the contract.The portfolio stretches past football. He bought into the WNBA's Las Vegas Aces in March 2023 and joined Birmingham City in August 2023, where he chairs the advisory board. A pickleball team and an E1 powerboat team came along too.Not every bet paid off. Autograph, his digital collectibles company, had to change direction, and his FTX investment lost money. TB12, his wellness brand, did find a buyer. The BRADY apparel line and the production company 199 Productions carry on.Net worth is harder to pin down. Published estimates run from $300 million to $650 million, depending on the tracker. None are audited, and most of his stakes are private.The field still tugs at him. He has said he weighed a comeback, though the NFL did not like the idea. A return would clash with both the Fox contract and his Raiders stake.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Maxx Crosby Hypes Fernando Mendoza After 1st Raiders Start, Reacts to Kirk Cousins' Trade to Vikings
articles.summary: Las Vegas Raiders star pass-rusher Maxx Crosby was excited about Fernando Mendoza's potential after the rookie quarterback made the first start of his career during the team's 21-13 loss to the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday.
articles.body:
Las Vegas Raiders star pass-rusher Maxx Crosby was excited about Fernando Mendoza's potential after the rookie quarterback made the first start of his career during the team's 21-13 loss to the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday.

"Fernando, that dude, he's a robot," Crosby said during Tuesday's episode of his podcast, The Rush with Maxx Crosby (4:59 mark). "You know what I mean? He does everything the right way. He's a great f--king kid. He's extremely talented, he's competitive and he's gonna be a great quarterback for a long time."

Mendoza became Las Vegas' starting signal-caller after the Raiders traded veteran passer Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings on Nov. 10.

While Cousins only suited up in nine games for Las Vegas, Crosby was appreciative of his tenure on the team.

"First and foremost, I'll forever love Kirk Cousins and he's good with me for life," Crosby said Tuesday (3:49 mark). "Such a good teammate, such a good dude, great quarterback playing incredible football right now. He was just the ultimate teammate, ultimate professional. He was a blessing to be around every single day. Everybody in that locker room loved him. He was such a good dude and such a great team guy. We wish him the best."

Cousins threw for 2,340 yards and 20 touchdowns compared to eight interceptions to open his 2026 campaign on the Raiders, but the 38-year-old was ultimately traded after the team fell to 4-5.

Mendoza, the No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NFL draft, took over under center on Sunday.

The 23-year-old finished 17-of-29 for 143 yards against Seattle, getting sacked six times. He also rushed for 22 yards on six attempts, finding the end zone once on the ground.

It was an encouraging performance from Mendoza, especially considering his first career start came against a Seahawks squad that's coming off a Super Bowl title and boasts one of the NFL's top secondaries.

Seattle owns the league's No. 1 pass defense this year, allowing a mere 149.4 yards through the air on a weekly basis.

As for Crosby, the five-time Pro Bowler has continued to make his presence felt as part of Las Vegas' defensive front in 2026. He's racked up 34 tackles, 21 quarterback hits, nine tackles for loss and five sacks in 10 games.

articles.title: Steelers rookie Max Iheanachor had home burglarized, $200,000 worth of property stolen during preseason game
articles.summary: An arrest warrant was issued on Tuesday for three men in connection with the incident, which occurred in August.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Police have issued arrest warrants for three people who allegedly burglarized the home of Pittsburgh Steelers rookie Max Iheanachor earlier this year, according to ESPN's Brooke Pryor .

The three men — Los Angeles residents Winter Brantley, 25, Andre Castle Jr., 23, and Lamar Stewart, 45 — allegedly broke into Iheanachor's home in August and stole more than $200,000 worth of jewelry and designer items. Iheanachor was not home at the time, and was instead in Buffalo for the Steelers' final preseason game against the Bills.

The three men are facing multiple charges of burglary, criminal trespass, theft by unlawful taking, receiving stolen property and conspiracy. Pittsburgh police are working with the U.S. Marshals Service to take the men into custody.

Brantley is the sister of Iheanachor's roommate, according to the report. The roommate, Ashley Brantley, told police last month that he had been "beefing" with his sister on and off over the past year, though the nature of that feud isn't known.

Iheanachor was selected with the No. 21 overall pick by the Steelers out of Arizona State earlier this year. He's started their past seven games at right tackle.

Iheanachor is just the latest professional athlete to face a situation like this in recent years. Dallas Cowboys star CeeDee Lamb had more than $300,000 worth of property stolen from his home during training camp earlier this year. New York Liberty guard Sabrina Ionescu had her Southern California home robbed in December, and Oklahoma City Thunder star Shai Gilgeous-Alexander had his home broken into in October. There were seven individuals charged earlier this year for allegedly burglarizing the homes of Patrick Mahomes, Travis Kelce and Joe Burrow, among others.

The Steelers sit at 6-3 on the season after Sunday night's 38-18 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals. They'll take on the Philadelphia Eagles next weekend.

articles.body:
One young Chicago sports star took home MVP this year, and now another is looking to do the same.

After Chicago Cubs outfielder Pete Crow-Armstrong was named MVP of the National League, Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams was asked if the city was big enough for two MVPs.

Crow-Armstrong, just 24 years old, is coming off a season in which he hit 45 homers and 107 RBI, also stealing 41 bases. He was the youngest player to be named MVP since Cody Bellinger won the award in 2019.

Williams is putting together a strong third season despite missing some time with a hamstring injury, throwing for 1,546 yards, eight touchdowns and five interceptions, leading the Bears to a 7-2 start.

Regardless of whether Williams can also take home MVP, it's an exciting time for Chicago sports fans, and Williams is embracing the relationship between the teams.

"That's one of the coolest things about being here in Chicago and what we're building here: It's not just Chicago Bears, it's us as Chicago athletes," Williams said Tuesday, per ESPN's Courtney Cronin . "We've talked about it multiple times, what we want to do for the city. This is just one of those stepping stones for Pete himself as his career goes, but also us as a friend group. We want to support each other, we want to show up for each other."

articles.title: Rich Eisen Reflects on His Return to ESPN and Planting More Flags For The Future
articles.summary: "After taking my show over in 2019 and building it, getting the opportunity to have that be the vehicle that returns me to ESPN, only to then have ESPN acqui...
articles.body:
Last year, Rich Eisen received a phone call he never imagined could happen. For the first time since 2003, the famed ESPN SportsCenter anchor returned to the place where his sports media career began its national rise. Twenty-two years after leaving to become the first personality on the NFL Network, Eisen returned with his own sports radio brand as The Rich Eisen Show joined ESPN Radio, with additional distribution on ESPN+ and Disney+.

Now, more than a year later, Eisen finds himself enjoying the opportunities his return to ESPN has provided. He has gained additional distribution, new teammates and opportunities to create original programming. Ultimately, Eisen says there is simply nothing like being back home with the worldwide leader in sports.

"I enjoy delivering the program into the ESPN, Disney+ sphere of influence and distribution. There is nothing like the ESPN platform. I experienced it from 1996-2003 as a host. But never thought my career would morph into host/small business owner," said Eisen. "After taking my show over in 2019 and building it, getting the opportunity to have that be the vehicle that returns me to ESPN, only to then have ESPN acquire my broadcasting rights from NFL Network. That's stuff you can't make up."

Eisen now serves in a hybrid role that combines elements of his previous ESPN experience with his current business ventures. He remains an on-air talent, hosting several programs on NFL Network throughout the calendar year, while also serving as the CEO and founder of Rich Eisen Productions.

The Rich Eisen Show remains Eisen's property. He still owns and produces the program, maintaining complete autonomy over its content. That was one of several promises ESPN made in its efforts to bring Eisen back home to the worldwide leader in sports.

"Everything I was promised I received in the first year, including support from ESPN digital and social platforms. Good Karma Sports selling my show and opening partnerships. Basically, fire hosing the show. They've done everything they say they would," noted Eisen. "It's been an awesome feeling."

Over the past year, Eisen has also had several opportunities to expand his presence under the ESPN umbrella. In April, he returned to ESPN's headquarters in Bristol, Connecticut, to host SportsCenter for the first time in more than two decades. He also worked with ESPN's archives on a podcast series that tapped into the nostalgia surrounding former SportsCenter anchors.

Most recently, ESPN announced that Eisen's radio program would expand its reach on Disney+. For the first time, The Rich Eisen Show would become available to international audiences through Disney+, with distribution in select countries across Europe, the Middle East and Africa (EMEA).

"I'm a professional flag planter. I was the first guy to be on the set of the NFL Network with a microphone. Everything NFL Network did growing up, any time we did something for the first time, I was thankfully handed the reins to lead it on air," said Eisen. "I planted flags for my show with DirecTV. Then I planted flags all over the place when I owned it. So, when ESPN wants to put my show and expand it on Disney+, great. I don't think about it as I have a lot of responsibilities. It's just what I'm used to doing."

For Eisen, expanding into international markets made complete sense. During his travels covering and calling NFL games overseas for NFL Network, he saw firsthand the interest and passion international audiences have for American football.

"I've seen the audience in Frankfurt, Munich, and London with my own two eyes," explained Eisen. "When we do a deal with my show with Disney and ESPN, they have worldwide rights. It makes sense for us to inquire about their expanding strategy, to see if we could get worldwide rights. To the credit of everyone at Disney+ and ESPN, they're up for it. Let's see how it works."

Calling NFL games overseas proved to be a rewarding experience for Eisen. He enjoyed more than the opportunity to broadcast the games themselves. He also embraced the atmosphere surrounding the events, from hosting The Rich Eisen Show on location to occasionally taking a Saturday stroll through a local beer garden.

However, 2026 brought a change. With ESPN overseeing NFL Network as part of its acquisition agreement with the NFL, Eisen's time calling the league's international series came to an end . He acknowledges that the assignment differed significantly from his typical responsibilities, but he admits he misses the experience.

"For the last year, ESPN and Disney provided our show a studio overseas. It was fun, we brought some of the staff. But, I got three kids at home and my role with NFL Network too," said Eisen. "But yes, I do miss it. One time in a week off between Frankfurt games, I went to Berlin and did a bike tour of the city because my wife insisted on getting out of the hotel when I was on my own. But, what a great experience overall."

Building For The Future, Leaning Into The Past

Above all, Eisen says he loves radio. He appreciates the opportunity to connect with people in real time and share conversations about their common passion for sports. He also recognizes how fortunate he is that the hard work of his entire team continues to earn support from the audience.

That connection gives Eisen a different sense of satisfaction from growing his radio program than he gets from anything he accomplishes on television.

"I'm growing a business. I have people that depend on me, and I depend on them. Having an outlet, I love having that and tracking our success on our platform," said Eisen. "On the television side of things, we're always looking for new ways to break down the fourth wall and connect with the fan and meet them where they are. Radio is the literal sense of meeting the fans where they are because they can connect with you from anywhere in real time."

Another way Eisen has strengthened that connection is through a podcast that tugs at the heartstrings of longtime SportsCenter viewers. For years, he wanted to develop a series that explored the stories behind the scenes and revisited memorable moments with the voices who once shared the desk on ESPN's flagship highlights program.

After noticing the growing popularity of nostalgia-driven podcasts, Eisen pitched the concept to ESPN President Jimmy Pitaro during discussions about his return to the network.

"With my show coming back into the orbit of ESPN, I thought this was the perfect opportunity to execute what I always been thinking about," said Eisen. "Jimmy [Pitaro] loved the idea, and we were off to the races."

With access to ESPN's SportsCenter archives, Eisen and his coordinating producer, Michael Hoskyns, went to work. Eisen reached out to former SportsCenter colleagues to discuss memorable moments from the past, while Hoskyns navigated the archives, identified footage and helped conceptualize the final product.

In June, This Was SportsCenter launched with six episodes featuring notable ESPN anchors from the past. The response was overwhelming, and Eisen is already planning a second season.

"I have a few things in the hopper for next year, including a book. I've already reached out to a bunch of my old school colleagues that I saved for a potential second season. Either because they were unable to do season one, or wanted to see the popularity of season one," explained Eisen. "Doing it in person is so much better than not. There's nothing like a face-to-face chat."

Eisen credits much of the series' appeal to how dramatically SportsCenter has changed over the years. Even today, fans approach him with memories of staying up late at night or beginning their mornings with Eisen and his longtime partner, Stuart Scott.

" SportsCenter , the way it used to be is different than the way it is today. That also applies to so much of sports television," said Eisen. "I hear stories from fans who remember me and Stuart Scott all the time. So, doing This Was SportsCente r, or occasionally popping on SportsCenter today, it's a lane that I'm pleased to have. With my radio show and all the distribution we have now, I can ask someone if they remember when I had hair and life was different for me and you. I'm thrilled ESPN allows me to occupy that lane."

This February, ESPN will broadcast its first Super Bowl in network history. The event will likely represent the largest and most consequential broadcast in the network's history. Eisen hinted that his show will have a presence throughout Super Bowl week and on game day, particularly with his home studio based in Los Angeles.

"ESPN is the greatest platform there is in sports and entertainment. I can only imagine it will be a Super Bowlpalooza," noted Eisen. "I look forward to being a part of it. My show will be connected and we're creating our own environment in my studio here in Los Angeles like we did for the last Super Bowl here. We have some other plans about the show that I imagine will be announced really soon. But I'm excited about it, and I'll be a part of the Super Bowlpalooza. Whether it's my show or NFL Network, or presumably both. I'm really excited about it."

For Eisen, returning to ESPN wasn't about revisiting the past or trying to recapture what he once had. It was about finding a new way to build on everything that came before.

From launching NFL Network to growing his own radio show, creating original programming and expanding into international markets, Eisen has spent his career embracing opportunities that once seemed unimaginable.

Now, with a Super Bowl on the horizon, the NFL Combine and Draft approaching, and new projects taking shape, his second act with ESPN is still being written. And if there's one thing Eisen has learned throughout his career, it's that there are always more flags to plant.

articles.title: George Pickens the Cowboys' shining light for a change in Week 10

This season, his 678 receiving yards and five receiving touchdowns rank twelfth in the NFL.
